properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-28, from the dev_reflow2 hub session, thinking out loud ("This is kind of an open ended brainstorm"). Nothing here is settled.

HIS WORDS: "I just recently went through massive review of 370 gaps on the storyflow project. I asked it to basically analyze all the gaps and determine a closure plan for them, then close them (there was a caveat of when to review again). That being said, I noticed on I have 87 "still to decide" and 125 What the design hasn't said yet and multiple proposed of the 83 requirements to build on flo2. I'm sure that if I looked on reflow2, it would be similarly daunting. I almost feel like we should have a "/step-back" skill that literally takes a step back and looks at the project again from a macro level and says "this is OBE now" or "these gaps can be closed easily" or "let's refocus on the most pressing things"".

THE IDEA: a periodic review of the whole open list that sorts it into three piles (overtaken by events, cheap to close, the few that matter now) instead of working it item by item. The neighbourhood half of what he said, focusing on a region rather than a thread, is its own question: dec:idea-the-unit-of-focus-is-a-region-of-the-design-not-a-thread.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (searched before writing, 2026-09-28):
- what_next ranks open decisions and names the shaping few, which is the existing big-picture read. It ranks single decisions, never piles.
- retire-from-design drops without deleting. dec:proposed-requirements-pruned (accepted, 2026-07-30) did one prune like this by hand: 9 of 26 proposed requirements retired.
- dec:idea-can-the-unaccepted-be-purged-in-bulk (2026-08-12) is the same pain six weeks earlier. Its measurement is the strongest input here: 26 of 47 proposed requirements were already satisfied. That was stale status, not surplus intent.
- One narrow detector for "overtaken" is built: an open question that its own promotion already answered is noticed.
- what_next's governs_retired says when most of what a settled decision shaped has since been pruned.
So a /step-back is mostly an ORCHESTRATION of reads that already exist, plus one pile nothing computes yet.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
A. A SKILL ONLY. Served text that runs the existing reads in order (stale status first, then overtaken, then closable, then refocus) and hands Anthony a short list of CLASSES to rule on. Cheapest by far: no engine change. Its limit: "this is OBE" stays the agent's judgement, argued per class.
B. A COMPUTED "overtaken candidates" read that joins signals the graph can already see: proposed requirements with a built, satisfying capability; open questions whose options were all superseded or promoted; decisions whose governed nodes are all dropped; gaps standing on withdrawn nodes. Medium: each signal exists separately, and one read would join them. Its limit: most "overtaken by events" is about events OUTSIDE the graph (a library shipped, the market moved, the owner changed his mind), and no computation sees those.
C. A NUDGE instead of a skill: when the open list crosses some size, loop_status suggests a step-back. Cheap to build. But every count threshold is one the design has refused to invent elsewhere, and dec:idea-a-project-says-what-it-is-doing-now-so-the-loop-stops-pushing (accepted) holds the invitation for a boundary, so the natural trigger is a boundary (a release cut, an increment closing), not a count.
D. NOTHING NEW. Run where-am-i, what_next and retire-from-design by hand. Free. Against it: he has now asked for this twice (the purge idea, then this), which says the existing route is not found at the moment it is needed.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea rather than used against it:
1. THE STORYFLOW PASS WAS ALREADY A STEP-BACK, and the counts are still large. Another agent pass of the same shape risks the same result. Whatever this becomes has to change the UNIT OF DECISION (a few classes, each ruled by Anthony) rather than run a longer pass.
2. IT CANNOT CLOSE ANYTHING ON ITS OWN. rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word and dec:bulk-keeps-the-judgement-per-item (both accepted) mean a step-back can only PROPOSE "overtaken" or "closable", and each item keeps its own reason. The saving is Anthony's time (ruling on about ten classes rather than about two hundred items), never skipped judgement.
3. BIG IS NOT ALWAYS WRONG. Per dec:gap-reporting-when-most-intent-is-unbuilt, on a design where most intent is not built yet, a large "not said yet" count is the honest state. A step-back that shrinks it by closing honest unbuilt intent hides the design instead of cleaning it. It has to tell "open because not reached yet" (leave it) from "open because stale or overtaken" (clear it).
4. THE "REVIEW AGAIN WHEN" CAVEATS. The storyflow closures carry prose conditions for when to look again. dec:idea-an-acknowledgement-cannot-state-its-own-expiry-condition records that nothing evaluates such a condition, so it reads as watched when it is not. A step-back is the natural place to re-read them. Without one, the conditions on 370 closures are exactly that trap.

CHEAPEST FIRST MOVE, if any is ever taken: the stale-status pile (option E of the purge idea). When measured it would have cut the proposed-requirement count by more than half, it drops nothing, and it needs only "yes, these are delivered".
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 have a /step-back review that looks at the whole design from a macro level and sorts what is open into overtaken, easily closed, and the few most pressing?
properties.rationale: Captured on Anthony's instruction to record the ideas as ideas, at proposed, in his words, with counter-arguments beside them and nothing promoted. Kept separate from the neighbourhood idea because the two can be answered independently: a step-back could refocus on single items, and a region focus could exist with no step-back. The existing pieces are named so that a later session argues from what is built rather than re-deriving it, and the purge idea's 26-of-47 measurement is carried forward because it says most of the felt weight may be stale status rather than surplus intent.
